To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cryptorchidism and hernia are important aetiological factors in testicular cancer, as are certain infections and immunological disorders, and that there is a dose-response relationship between the severity of cryptorchid testes and the risk of testicular neoplasia.
the risk of testicular germ cell tumours is raised for men with histories of cryptorchid testes, mumps orchitis, atopy, and meningitis.
the risk of testicular germ cell cancer was raised for men who had a history of: (i) cryptorchidism; (ii) mumps orchitis; (iii) atopy; (iv) inguinal herniorrhapy; and (v) meningitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the aetiology, diagnosis, and treatment of testicular cancer.
the identification of risk factors for testis cancer, and the elucidation of possible mechanisms by which these factors may increase risk.
the epidemiology of cancer of the testis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
testicular cancer is caused by a complex combination of genetic, developmental and immunological factors, but that these factors may not be mutually exclusive.

cryptorchidism, inguinal herniorrhapy, and mumps orchitis are risk factors for all types of testis cancer, while atopy, meningitis and possibly also inguinal hernias are also risk factors, but only for seminoma.

testicular cancer is associated with a number of conditions that may be related to abnormal testicular development, and with a number of infections and other conditions that may be associated with immunodeficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
testicular damage of any type, occurring before or after puberty, may be an important aetiological factor for testicular cancer.

the aetiological factors for testicular tumours are likely to include congenital abnormalities of testicular descent, infections of the testis (particularly mumps orchitis), and possibly immunological abnormalities.
testicular cancer is a disease with a multifactorial aetiology, involving both congenital and acquired factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
testicular cancer can be caused by a variety of factors, and that there are several different types of testicular cancer.
the risk of testicular germ cell cancer is increased in men with a history or cryptorchidism, inguinal hernias and mumps orchitis.
there is a link between testicular cancer and cryptorchidism, inguinal hernias and orchitis.
